ION Clean Energy 30 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT Figure 9-3: ICE-21™ Samples During the Second Week of Operations Despite the elevated DCC operating temperatures (>115 °F), ION observed minimal degradation in the ICE-21™ solvent over the first two months of operations (~90 tCO captured). 2 9.3 ICE-31® ION operated for 6200 hours with ICE-31® from February 2024 to February 2025. ION captured 2479 tonnes of CO during the ICE-31® campaign. ION performed 2265 hours of parametric testing from 2 February 2024 to July 2024. This was followed by nearly 4000 hours of long-term steady-state testing concluding in February 2025. 9.3.1 Optimal L/G at 95% Capture ION varied the L/G ratio at 95-96% CO capture to determine optimal performance of the solvent. 2 L/G is calculated based on the lean solvent flow rate and the flue gas flow rate into the absorber. For each setpoint, ION modeled the steam duty needed for 95% capture prior to changing operating conditions. The actual ENTP steam load was then set at a determined flow rate, and the capture efficiency was allowed to reach a steady state. Due to the high accuracy of the ProTreat® model, the resulting capture efficiency at ENTP was almost always within the range of the target capture rate, allowing relatively smooth and quick transitions between setpoints. The optimal lean loading is a balance between increasing the carrying capacity of the solvent to limit sensible heat loss in the lean/rich cross exchanger and increasing lean loading in the stripper bottoms to better utilize stripping steam. ION found the optimal performance to be at 0.71 lb/lb, however the SRD remains within 5% of the minimum in the range of 0.63 to 0.87 lb/lb. This optimal range is reflective of both the ProTreat® modelling predictions and the design case of the ENTP facility. Heat loss is integrated into the SRD calculation. 9.3.2 SRD Increase with Capture Efficiency ION varied the capture efficiency at ENTP while choosing optimal L/G ratios to determine minimum SRD performance at each capture efficiency. The overall impact of the fast kinetics and favorable thermodynamics of ION’s ICE-31® solvent demonstrate that there is approximately a 6% SRD penalty when increasing capture from 90% to 98%. The impact on SRD going from 89% capture to 96% capture is minimal (approximately 1.8% increase), indicating that the solvent is reaching a similar rich loading at these capture efficiencies. However, beyond 96% capture, the solvent did not reach its optimal rich loading, leading to an increase in SRD at very high capture efficiencies.
